scope_contract.goal_statement: The Non-C2 JU wants to receive situational awareness data from the Surveillance NPG—including track and Reference Point data for air, surface (maritime), and land (ground) surveillance—in order to gain situational awareness and early warning information that supports its platform mission.

claims.content: The main flow begins with the Non-C2 JU receiving situational awareness data from the Surveillance NPG in the form of J3 series track reports (including subsurface maritime tracks) and Reference Point data for air, surface (maritime), land (ground), and subsurface surveillance domains, while monitoring this NPG without transmitting.
C2 JUs transmit J3 series surveillance messages containing track and Reference Point data on the Surveillance NPG.

The Non-C2 JU receives situational awareness data from the Surveillance NPG in the form of J3 series track reports (including subsurface maritime tracks) and Reference Point data for air, surface (maritime), land (ground), and subsurface surveillance domains.
The received track data include J3.2 Air Track, J3.3 Surface (Maritime) Track, and J3.5 Land (Ground) Point/Track messages.

The Non-C2 JU relinquishes R² for a real-time air, surface, or land track when a received remote track report has a remote TQ greater than the local TQ, or has an equal TQ from a JU whose STN is greater than the local STN.
The Non-C2 JU obtains situational awareness and early warning information from the received remote surveillance track and point data in the J3 series messages, supporting its platform mission.
Diverges from Step 4: The situational awareness data received by the Non-C2 JU may include reporting of inactive sites as Air and Surface (Maritime) Tracks and Land (Ground) Track Data.

Diverges from Step 3: A received track report may be identified as a nonreal-time report with the TQ field set to value 0 when the track data originate from other than a TDS or JTIDS/MIDS equipped aircraft, have been relayed from another system by other than a real-time data link interface, or have been derived from other than integrated sensors.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Non-C2 JU has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface (Maritime) track for approximately 40 seconds, or on a locally held Land (Ground) track for approximately 120 seconds, it assumes R² for that track.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Non-C2 JU receives a J2 PPLI message from a JU that has R² of a locally held track, with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure, it may assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Non-C2 JU does not have R² for a nonreal-time track with the TQ field set to value 0, it assumes R² for that track when the track is locally updated by a new nonreal-time report; the time value in the report is not a criterion for the R² shift.
Diverges from Step 5: The Non-C2 JU assumes R² if it has local real-time data and nonreal-time data were received.

claims.content: At main-flow Step 1, if the Non-C2 JU would transmit on the Surveillance NPG, the attempted transmission is prohibited: Non-C2 JUs shall not transmit on the Surveillance NPG.

At main-flow Step 2, if a JU would report a TQ value whose associated positional accuracy is better than that associated with its own unit's current geodetic position quality, it shall not report that TQ value.

At main-flow Step 3, if the JU receiving the J2 finds a correlation with a track for which another C2 JU has R² and the Track Numbers are the same, it shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on that track; however, if the Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message is discarded instead.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_trigger_continuity] Main Flow step 1 already continues from the Trigger by showing the Non-C2 JU receiving the J3 data. Step 2 then jumps back to the pre-trigger condition that C2 JUs transmit those J3 messages on the Surveillance NPG, and step 3 repeats the receipt from step 1. This creates a backward jump/restart instead of a forward continuous flow from the Trigger. (coverage-preserving removal: not subsumed (The witness claim describes Non-C2 JUs receiving J3 series track reports and Reference Point data while monitoring, and explicitly says they do not transmit. It does not state that C2 JUs transmit J3 surveillance messages containing track and Reference Point data on the Surveillance NPG.))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] Main Flow step 1 already continues from the Trigger by showing the Non-C2 JU receiving the J3 data. Step 2 then jumps back to the pre-trigger condition that C2 JUs transmit those J3 messages on the Surveillance NPG, and step 3 repeats the receipt from step 1. This creates a backward jump/restart instead of a forward continuous flow from the Trigger.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger is defined as receipt of situational awareness data from the Surveillance NPG, but Main Flow step 1 has the Non-C2 JU monitoring the NPG and step 2 has C2 JUs transmitting before step 3 repeats the receipt. Monitoring and C2 transmission are pre-trigger states/events, so the Main Flow restarts before the Trigger instead of continuing from it.
